subject: Learning Methods
title: The Encoding Benefit
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Encoding Benefit.

hook.text: Students who took notes during a lecture remembered more than those who listened, even if they never reviewed the notes.

buildup.text: The act of note-taking forces you to select, process, and rephrase information.

discovery.text: This is the encoding benefit: the process of writing notes strengthens memory independent of whether you ever reread.

twist.text: Verbatim transcription skips this benefit. Copying word-for-word requires no processing, so it encodes almost nothing.

climax.text: Take notes in your own words. The translation from source language to personal language is where the learning happens.

punchline.text: Writing notes teaches you. Even if you never read them again.

quiz.question: Why does verbatim transcription provide little encoding benefit?
options: Copying word-for-word requires no mental processing
Transcription is faster than the brain can encode
